environment: Two disposable Linux ARM64 Podman VMs sequentially, each 1 CPU and 2 GiB RAM; local XFS; stopped and removed

direct.observed: Reserved dash, whitespace and non-ASCII IDs and malformed JSON were refused; voter and group watermark remained unchanged. A valid ID persisted in both. Bypassing the group ID precheck advanced the watermark. Bypassing the reserved-dash check and its fixture assertion made a native voter write the inconsistent state `1 - 0 - -`. Topology-member predicate was stubbed.

integration.observed: Three native group servers with synthetic HMAC token and signed test topology chose epochs 1 and 2. After one server was killed, the remaining quorum retained epoch 1. With another epoch-1 state file removed, the proposer returned no majority and that file was not recreated.

limits: The test uses one VM, synthetic credentials and test data. It does not qualify external monotonic state, rollback prevention, multi-host failure isolation, Mac runtime, real inference, power loss or full resident operation.
